paragraphs.en: Kamola needed an overall band of 7.0 to apply for a master's programme in the Netherlands. The first time she took IELTS, she scored 6.0. She was disappointed but not surprised: she had spent most of her preparation doing practice tests, one after another, without really analysing her mistakes.
paragraphs.uz: Niderlandiyadagi magistratura dasturiga hujjat topshirish uchun Kamolaga umumiy 7.0 ball kerak edi. IELTS'ni birinchi marta topshirganida, u 6.0 oldi. U hafsalasi pir bo'ldi, lekin hayron bo'lmadi: u tayyorgarlikning katta qismini xatolarini chuqur tahlil qilmasdan, ketma-ket sinov testlarini yechish bilan o'tkazgandi.

paragraphs.en: For her second attempt, she changed her approach. Instead of doing more tests, she kept a "mistake diary". Every wrong answer in reading and listening went into it, together with the reason: Did she misread the question? Miss a paraphrase? Run out of time? After a month, a clear pattern emerged — most of her errors came from not recognising synonyms.
paragraphs.uz: Ikkinchi urinish uchun u yondashuvini o'zgartirdi. Ko'proq test yechish o'rniga u "xatolar kundaligi" yuritdi. Reading va listening'dagi har bir noto'g'ri javob sababi bilan birga unga yozilardi: savolni noto'g'ri o'qidimi? Parafrazni payqamadimi? Vaqti yetmadimi? Bir oydan keyin aniq qonuniyat ko'rindi — xatolarining aksariyati sinonimlarni tanimaslikdan kelib chiqqan edi.

paragraphs.en: Her second result was 6.5, with 7.5 in reading but only 6.0 in writing. The examiner's comments were blunt: her essays were well organised, but her vocabulary was repetitive and her ideas were too general. "Many people believe that..." appeared in almost every paragraph.
paragraphs.uz: Ikkinchi natijasi 6.5 bo'ldi: reading'dan 7.5, lekin writing'dan atigi 6.0. Imtihonchining izohlari to'g'ridan-to'g'ri edi: inshoalari yaxshi tuzilgan, lekin lug'ati takroriy, g'oyalari esa juda umumiy edi. "Many people believe that..." deyarli har bir paragrafda uchrardi.

paragraphs.en: So she spent three months focusing almost entirely on writing. She read opinion articles every morning and noted how journalists supported their arguments with specific examples. She also asked a teacher to mark one essay a week, and rewrote each essay after receiving feedback. Had she not rewritten them, she says, she would have kept making the same mistakes.
paragraphs.uz: Shuning uchun u uch oy deyarli faqat writing'ga e'tibor qaratdi. Har kuni ertalab fikr-mulohaza maqolalarini o'qib, jurnalistlar o'z dalillarini aniq misollar bilan qanday qo'llab-quvvatlashini yozib bordi. Shuningdek, u o'qituvchidan haftada bitta inshoni tekshirib berishni so'radi va izoh olgach har bir inshoni qayta yozdi. Uning aytishicha, ularni qayta yozmaganida, bir xil xatolarni takrorlashda davom etgan bo'lardi.

paragraphs.en: On her third attempt, Kamola got 7.5 overall, with 7.0 in writing. Looking back, she thinks the score mattered less than the lesson: "Doing more isn't the same as improving. You improve when you find out exactly why you're failing — and then work on that one thing."
paragraphs.uz: Uchinchi urinishda Kamola umumiy 7.5, writing'dan esa 7.0 oldi. O'tmishga nazar tashlab, u balldan ko'ra olingan saboq muhimroq deb hisoblaydi: "Ko'proq qilish — yaxshilanish degani emas. Nima uchun aynan muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrayotganingizni aniqlab, keyin aynan shu narsa ustida ishlaganingizdagina o'sasiz."

questions.q: What was wrong with Kamola's first preparation?
options: She didn't do any practice tests.
She did many tests but didn't analyse her mistakes.

questions.q: What did her mistake diary show?
options: She often ran out of time.
Most errors came from not recognising synonyms.

questions.q: What did the examiner criticise in her writing?
Which statement best summarises Kamola's lesson?
options: Take the exam as many times as possible.
Find the exact cause of your weakness and work on it.
Writing is the easiest part of IELTS.
